subject: Money
title: Inflation Psychology
description: A short lesson to help you apply Inflation Psychology.

hook.text: When gas prices jump, people feel poorer even if their overall spending barely changes. Psychology trumps math.

buildup.text: Inflation expectations drive behavior. If people think prices will rise 5%, they spend now and demand higher wages.

discovery.text: Anchored expectations keep inflation stable. If everyone believes 2%, wage demands and pricing stay moderate.

twist.text: Social media amplifies inflation anxiety. One viral post about egg prices shapes perception more than CPI data.

climax.text: Managing inflation is as much about managing belief as managing money supply. Perception is half the battle.

punchline.text: Believe prices will rise. Make them rise.

quiz.question: Why are inflation expectations important?
options: They influence spending and wage demands, becoming self-fulfilling
